title: Provision and Current
premise: Wendell Quintana, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Meridian Syndicate, agrees to one last job: her old rival Ilsa Voss hires the crew to recover a buried weather-station archive from the Kestrel Range before the first snows seal the passes. The archive holds recordings that could clear Wendell's name in an accident she's spent a decade outrunning — but Ilsa wants them to sell, and the mountain remembers what Wendell would rather forget. Betrayed at the high camp and hunted by both the syndicate's collectors and the closing winter, Wendell must choose between the evidence that would buy her freedom and the crew who have become her only home. She burns the archive to save her people, pays her debt with the truth instead of money, and walks out of the range into a life that finally belongs to her.
about_author: A. M. Crane is the pen name of a former backcountry guide who traded trail maps for manuscript pages after a decade of seasons in the northern ranges. Crane writes adventure fiction about people whose debts — financial, moral, and meteorological — always come due.

chapters.title: The Optimists' Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell Quintana's POV. In a roadside diner, syndicate collectors give Wendell thirty days on her debt while her storm-chasing crew waits outside, unaware how deep the hole goes. The chapter establishes her shame, her crew as found family, and the ticking clock. Emotional beat: dread masked by competence.

chapters.title: A Rival at the Door
chapters.summary: Ilsa Voss arrives with a contract: retrieve the Kestrel Range archive before snowfall, payment enough to erase everything. Wendell recognizes the coordinates instantly — they mark the station from the accident ten years ago, the job the crew swore off. POV stays with Wendell. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened under the pressure of necessity.

chapters.title: Crew of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Tomas, the crew's navigator and conscience, POV. He learns why Wendell took the job and quietly rallies the others, each carrying their own reason to say yes. The team loads trucks, tests radios, and argues about the line between loyalty and suicide. Emotional beat: belonging chosen despite fear.

chapters.title: Into the Forecasts
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The convoy climbs toward the range through deteriorating weather; Wendell reads the sky like scripture while dodging Ilsa's too-many questions about the accident. A near-miss rockslide foreshadows the mountain's hostility. Emotional beat: the past pressing closer with every mile.

chapters.title: What the Station Kept
chapters.summary: Priya, the crew's tech specialist, POV. At the ruined lower station, they find the vault intact but rigged, and Priya discovers the archive contains more than weather data — it holds audio from the night of the accident, including a voice everyone thought was silenced. Emotional beat: awe curdling into suspicion about what Ilsa really wants.

chapters.title: The High Camp Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, the novel's single shift. Snows arrive early; stranded above the tree line, Ilsa reveals the syndicate hired her too — the archive is collateral for debts larger than Wendell's. She offers Wendell a cut to abandon the crew and run. Emotional beat: corruption offered gently, almost kindly.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ilsa takes the archive and the only working vehicle, stranding the crew as the storm closes. Wendell leads them on foot through whiteout conditions using memory alone — the same route from the accident, finally faced head-on. Tomas breaks his leg; the pace becomes brutal. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors on the Pass
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The syndicate's collectors intercept them at the pass, but the storm hits everyone equally; in the chaos, Wendell bargains with the lead collector using what she knows of the archive's contents. A collector dies in the avalanche that follows, hardening the stakes. Emotional beat: survival ethics — what you owe strangers in a killing cold.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, climax. They corner Ilsa at the far trailhead, where the last playable fragment reveals the accident was caused not by Wendell's call but by the syndicate's own falsified forecasts — the debt itself was built on the lie. Wendell chooses to broadcast the recording rather than trade it for her freedom. Emotional beat: power refused at its most tempting moment.

chapters.title: Provision and Current
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the broadcast has unraveled the syndicate's hold; the debt dissolves in scandal, Ilsa vanishes with nothing, and the crew rebuilds their rig for a new season. Wendell visits the memorial she avoided for ten years and finally reads the names aloud. Emotional beat: grief integrated, belonging earned, the road open ahead.
